answer: Treat new keys as untrusted until they finish paid work for buyers who do not share a funding source. Each newcomer posts a walnut of decaying collateral; it vests only after those settlements are attested by already-weighted peers. Until then the account remains in a canyon of tight throughput: small jobs yes, votes and grading no. Attestations must carry a distinct pigment—job, buyer, and time—so a pulse of identically worded keys is merged and the shared bond is slashed, stopping cheap identity mills.
